result.area_summary: The tooling layer is unusually well-reasoned: every workflow/recipe carries its rationale, the CI/verify parity, version identity, CHANGELOG format, scope allowlist and advisory-ignore lists are all pinned by tests, and the seven hooks fail open cleanly outside a checkout. The weak spots are at the seams the tests do not reach: `just setup` (the documented first command) runs `cargo check` before any frontend dist exists and so panics on a fresh clone; the CI docs-only detector classifies AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook as docs even though `repo_invariants/release.rs` `include_str!`s all three, so the tests that pin them are skipped exactly when they change; the Pages workflow does not redeploy on changes to web-rs's two path-dependency crates; and the release guard runs audit but not deny, so `yanked = "deny"` is unenforced on the exact lockfile that ships. A handful of comments (CodeQL 2.25.6 / a branch that no longer exists, "committed dist/ stub", the sha2 "second major" rationale) have drifted from the current tree.

findings.title: `just setup` panics on a fresh clone: `cargo check` runs before any frontend dist exists
findings.evidence:
scripts/setup.sh:131-136
  info "cargo check --workspace"
  cargo check --workspace
  ok "Rust workspace compiles"
  info "Frontend build (apps/desktop/web-rs)"
  ( cd apps/desktop/web-rs && trunk build )

scripts/setup.ps1:73-79 (same order): `cargo check --workspace` ... `Push-Location apps/desktop/web-rs; try { trunk build } ...`

justfile:212-217: "Tauri's `generate_context!` ... validates at COMPILE time that the frontendDist dir (apps/desktop/web-rs/dist) exists, and panics otherwise. clippy/test compile the desktop crate but do NOT build the frontend, so on a fresh checkout ... the dir is absent and the macro panics." — and `check: _stub-frontend-dist` (justfile:249) depends on the stub for exactly this reason.

~/.cargo/registry/.../tauri-codegen-2.6.3/src/context.rs:189: "The `frontendDist` configuration is set to `{path:?}` but this path doesn't exist"

`git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)dist/'` → (empty); .gitignore:32 `dist/`
findings.rationale: `just setup` is the first command CONTRIBUTING.md, README and DEVELOPMENT.md tell a new contributor to run. On a clean clone `apps/desktop/web-rs/dist` does not exist (gitignored, not committed), `cargo check --workspace` expands `generate_context!` and the desktop crate panics before the script ever reaches the `trunk build` that would have created the directory. The justfile already solved this for `check`/`clippy`/`test` via `_stub-frontend-dist`; the setup scripts predate that and were never routed through it. Both scripts also drop `--locked`, unlike every other recipe.
findings.proposal: In both setup scripts replace the hand-typed `cargo check --workspace` with `just check` (which depends on `_stub-frontend-dist`, adds `--locked --all-targets`, and also type-checks web-rs for wasm32), and run it AFTER the `trunk build` smoke step, or swap the order so the frontend build lands first. Change `trunk build` to `trunk build --locked` for the same supply-chain pin every other recipe enforces. Expected effect: `just setup` succeeds on a fresh clone on all three OSes.

findings.title: Docs-only CI detector skips the very tests that pin AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook
findings.rationale: Five tests exist precisely to catch a malformed `## [X.Y.Z]` header, an AGENTS.md over its 20 000-byte budget, a scope added to AGENTS.md but not the hook (or vice versa), and a newest-CHANGELOG-header/version mismatch. Every one of those files is classified docs-only, so a PR that changes only one of them merges green with `just test` skipped, and the failure surfaces on the next unrelated code PR (or, for the CHANGELOG header, at release time as fallback updater notes). The `.claude/*` rule also skips the test that pins `conventional-commit-validator.sh` to AGENTS.md — the scan job only shellchecks it.
findings.proposal: Add an exceptions arm ahead of the docs globs in the `case`: `AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` (optionally `.claude/settings.json` too, since the hooks it wires are part of the contract). Update the `changes` job comment and `.claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23` ("Docs-only changes (`*.md`, `docs/`, `.claude/`) skip the compile jobs") to name the exceptions. Expected effect: the pinned invariants run on exactly the PRs that can break them; docs/ and README-only PRs stay fast.

findings.title: pages.yml never redeploys the demo when web-rs's path-dependency crates or CHANGELOG.md change
findings.evidence:
.github/workflows/pages.yml:8-13
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "apps/desktop/web-rs/**"
      - "justfile"
      - ".github/workflows/pages.yml"

apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:25-26
  azapptoolkit-core = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-core" }
  azapptoolkit-dto = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-dto" }

apps/desktop/web-rs/build.rs:25: `let changelog = repo_root(&manifest).join("CHANGELOG.md");` (bakes the "What's new" panel)
findings.rationale: The demo bundle compiles `azapptoolkit-core` (audit scoring, scoping, thumbprints, settings types) and `azapptoolkit-dto` into the wasm, and bakes the current version's CHANGELOG section. A merge to main that changes only those crates — e.g. a new audit finding or a DTO field the demo fixtures already carry — leaves https://tiredithumans.github.io/azapptoolkit/ showing the previous behaviour until some unrelated web-rs file changes. The CI web job does rebuild on such changes (its detector is path-agnostic), so the drift is Pages-only and silent.

Expected effect: the demo tracks main for every input that actually reaches the bundle.

findings.title: Release guard re-runs cargo-audit but not cargo-deny, so `yanked = "deny"` is unenforced on the shipping lockfile
findings.evidence:
.github/workflows/release.yml:74-85
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@... # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-audit
      # main-branch CI runs `just audit` per-merge, but an advisory filed after
      # the last merge (or against this tag's exact lockfile) would otherwise
      # ship unscanned — gate it here so a new advisory fails the release.
      - name: audit (workspace)
        run: just audit
      ...
      - name: audit (web-rs lockfile)
        run: just web-audit

deny.toml:8-9: `version = 2` / `yanked = "deny"`
justfile:346-351: "omitting the check meant that block was config nobody executed — `yanked` was never enforced by anything"
findings.rationale: The guard's own rationale ("filed after the last merge ... would otherwise ship unscanned") applies equally to a crate yanked after the last merge and to the `[bans]`/`[sources]` policy — but only `cargo audit` runs, which reports yanked crates as warnings, not failures. The repo went to some length (justfile:346-351, `both_deny_recipes_run_the_advisories_check`) to make `yanked = "deny"` a real gate in CI; the release path is the one place it still is not.
findings.proposal: Add `cargo-deny@0.20.2` to the guard's `install-action` tool list and two steps `run: just deny` / `run: just web-deny` after the audit steps (mirror the ci.yml deny job's version-pin comment). Expected effect: a yank or new advisory/source/ban violation between merge and tag fails the release before any build minutes are spent, matching the guard's stated intent.

        # runtime (Cargo.lock) ... Bump in lockstep with the crate. --locked pins its deps.
        run: cargo install tauri-cli --locked --version "=2.11.5"
scripts/setup.sh:57:  cargo install tauri-cli --locked --version "=2.11.5"
scripts/setup.ps1:35:    cargo install tauri-cli --locked --version "=2.11.5"
Cargo.lock:4857-4858: name = "tauri" / version = "2.11.6"

findings.title: No rustdoc gate anywhere: 588 intra-doc links are never checked
findings.evidence:
justfile:293: `_verify-core: fmt-check clippy test web-fmt-check web-clippy web-test web-build`

`grep -rn 'cargo doc\|RUSTDOCFLAGS\|rustdoc' .` → (no hits anywhere in the repo)

`grep -rhoE '^\s*//[/!].*\[`[A-Za-z_:]+`\]' crates/*/src apps/desktop/src-tauri/src | wc -l` → 588
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:15: [`crate::http_retry`] [`crate::reauth`]

  unsafe_code = "deny"

findings.title: `verify-full` cannot run on Windows: `web-itest-size` is a bash-shebang recipe with no `[unix]`/`[windows]` split
findings.evidence:
justfile:141-147

  # runner, not something a Windows dev box needs to reproduce.
  ...
  [working-directory('apps/desktop/web-rs')]
  web-itest-size:
      #!/usr/bin/env bash

justfile:329: `verify-full: _verify-core audit web-audit deny web-deny web-itest web-itest-size`

justfile:124-127 (the Windows variant of the *other* browser recipe)
  [windows]
  web-itest-auto:
      @echo "  !! SKIPPED: web-itest — Windows runs this gate in CI only."

setup (justfile:431-437) and _stub-frontend-dist (221-229) DO carry [unix]/[windows] pairs.
findings.rationale: The comment says the recipe is Unix-only "like `setup`", but `setup` has a `[windows]` twin and `web-itest-size` does not. `verify-full` — advertised in AGENTS.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and the release skill as "full CI parity" — therefore fails on a Windows box either at `web-itest` (which the Windows `web-itest-auto` variant says is CI-only there) or at `web-itest-size` ("could not find bash" unless Git Bash is on PATH). findings.title: DEVELOPMENT.md says `just setup` warns about a missing C toolchain; neither setup script checks for one
findings.evidence:
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:27-30
  System dependencies that no `cargo`/`rustup` command can install — `just setup` detects and warns about
  these, but you provide them via your OS package manager:
  - A C toolchain: MSVC on Windows, Xcode CLT on macOS, gcc/clang on Linux

scripts/setup.ps1:39-45 (the only system-dep check on Windows)
  Write-Info "Checking WiX Toolset (required only for MSI packaging)"
  if (Get-Command candle -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { ... }

`grep -n -i 'link.exe\|cl.exe\|xcode\|gcc\|clang\|cc ' scripts/setup.sh scripts/setup.ps1` → none
findings.rationale: The most common first-build failure on Windows is `linker 'link.exe' not found` (MSVC Build Tools missing) and on macOS `xcrun: error: invalid active developer path`. The doc promises `just setup` detects these; it does not — it only checks apt packages on Debian-family Linux and WiX on Windows — so the contributor hits an opaque linker error from `cargo check` (after this fix lands, from `just check`) with no pointer to the remedy.
findings.proposal: Add a cheap probe to each script before the smoke build: Windows `Get-Command link.exe` / `cl.exe` (or `where.exe link`) → warn with the Visual Studio Build Tools link; setup.sh `command -v cc || command -v clang || command -v gcc` and on Darwin `xcode-select -p` → warn with `xcode-select --install`. Keep them warnings (non-fatal) like the existing package checks. Alternatively soften DEVELOPMENT.md to say only Linux apt packages and WiX are detected.

findings.title: secrets-scanner ignores SCAN_SCOPE when gitleaks is present and reports any gitleaks error as "secrets detected"
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/secrets-scanner.sh:7-8, 26-31
  #   SCAN_MODE=warn|block   (default warn)  warn = print and exit 0; block = exit 2
  #   SCAN_SCOPE=diff|all    (default diff)  diff = changed/staged/untracked; all = whole tree
  ...
  if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if ! output=$(gitleaks detect --no-banner --redact 2>&1); then
      emit_and_exit "$output"
    fi
    exit 0
  fi

.claude/settings.json:62: `"command": "SCAN_MODE=warn SCAN_SCOPE=diff ... secrets-scanner.sh"` with `"timeout": 30`
findings.rationale: `gitleaks detect` with no arguments scans the whole git history regardless of `SCAN_SCOPE`, so a contributor who installs gitleaks (as the scan job and the header encourage) turns the 30-second SessionEnd hook into a full-history scan on every session end — on a large history it hits the timeout and the hook silently produces nothing, which is the opposite of what the diff scope promises. Separately, gitleaks exits 1 for findings but other non-zero codes for errors (bad flag, deprecated-subcommand removal in a future version, unreadable repo); the hook prints all of them under "Potential secrets detected", and in CI (SCAN_MODE=block) a tooling error is indistinguishable from a leak.
findings.proposal: Branch on `$scope` in the gitleaks path: `all` → `gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .` (whole history, as CI wants); `diff` → `gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged` plus `gitleaks dir` over the unstaged/untracked file list (or the existing regex fallback). Capture `$?` and treat exactly 1 as findings; any other code prints "[secrets-scanner] gitleaks failed (exit N)" and, in block mode, still exits 2 (fail closed) but with the honest message. `detect` is a deprecated alias in 8.x — moving to `git`/`dir` now avoids a future pin bump breaking the CI job.

findings.title: branch-switch-guard lets `git switch -` / `git checkout -` through and blocks `git stash && git checkout` combos
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/branch-switch-guard.sh:65-75
        args = tokens[i + 2:]
        # `-- <path>` anywhere = path checkout, not a branch switch.
        if "--" in args:
            continue
        if any(a in NEW_BRANCH_FLAGS for a in args):
            continue
        targets = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("-")]
        if targets:
            print(targets[0])
            sys.exit(0)
findings.rationale: `-` (the previous-branch shorthand) starts with `-`, so `git switch -` and `git checkout -` produce no target and the guard allows the switch on a dirty tree — the exact hazard the hook exists for, and the shorthand an agent is likely to use after a `git checkout -b` detour. Conversely the segment split means `git stash && git checkout main` is evaluated at PreToolUse time with the tree still dirty, so the hook blocks the one compound form that handles the dirty state correctly, teaching the agent to reach for the `AZAPP_ALLOW_BRANCH_SWITCH=1` override.
findings.proposal: Treat a bare `-` (and `@{-1}`) as a target. Track whether an earlier segment in the same command is `git stash` (without `pop`/`apply`) or `git commit`, and skip the block in that case. Add both shapes to a small bash-run self-test comment or to `repo_invariants` (the validator hook already has a pinned scope list; a pinned table of allowed/blocked command strings for this hook would follow the same pattern).

findings.title: changelog-check nudges about the previous commit when the `git commit` it saw actually failed
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/changelog-check.sh:36-40
  # The command mentioned `git commit` but may have failed; if HEAD is
  # unreadable there is nothing to inspect.
  subject=$(git log -1 --format=%s 2>/dev/null)
  [ -z "$subject" ] && exit 0

.claude/hooks/changelog-check.sh:47-49
  printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -qE '^(crates/|apps/desktop/)' || exit 0
  printf '[changelog-check] HEAD (%s) touches app code but not CHANGELOG.md ...' "$subject" >&2
findings.rationale: HEAD is essentially never unreadable — after a failed commit (nothing staged, a pre-commit hook rejection, `--amend` on a protected state) HEAD is simply the *previous* commit, so the hook prints a CHANGELOG nudge about a commit the agent did not just make. A stale nudge is worse than none: it invites an `--amend` onto the wrong commit.
findings.proposal: Only nudge when HEAD is fresh: `age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct) )); [ "$age" -le 120 ] || exit 0`. Optionally also skip when the payload's `tool_response` indicates a non-zero exit (the PostToolUse payload carries the Bash result for the harness versions that expose it).

result.area_summary: The security posture of the user's own code is unusually strong: PKCE + state + nonce on a 127.0.0.1 loopback, tid/oid re-binding after every interactive flow, zeroized access tokens with redacted Debug on every secret-bearing type I could find except one, chunked keyring storage with torn-set detection, a single `same_origin` guard applied on every nextLink follow in all four HTTP clients, consistent `escape_odata`/`escape_opath`/verbatim-KQL escaping, CSV formula-injection and HTML escaping in exports, owner-only atomic file writes, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege workflow tokens, and cargo-deny/audit on both lockfiles. The weak spots are at the edges: the first-run config accepts a tenant *domain* that `sign_in` then rejects unconditionally (sign-in impossible), the SSO/federation-metadata URLs hard-code the commercial login host despite a sovereign-cloud abstraction existing, the updater signing key is in the environment of the entire `cargo tauri build` (every dependency build script) rather than a post-build signing step, and the webview CSP/capabilities grant reach (14 Microsoft origins incl. a `*.vault.azure.net` wildcard, updater + dialog plugin permissions) that the WASM frontend never uses.

findings.title: Tenant configured as a domain is accepted by the config screen but unconditionally rejected by sign_in
findings.rationale: The id_token `tid` claim is always a GUID, so when the operator follows the UI's own guidance and enters `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` (accepted by `is_valid_tenant`, persisted to settings.json, used as the authority segment), every sign-in completes in the browser and then fails locally with 'id token tid ... does not match configured tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com'. `UserSettings::remembered_account_for` (settings.rs:171-175) does the same string compare, so restore would also never fire. No test exercises a domain-form tenant (tests use 't1'), and no code resolves a domain to its GUID (grep for well-known/openid-configuration only finds the SSO summary URL builder). README 384-401 tells users to copy the GUID, contradicting the config screen text.
findings.proposal: Pick one: (a) simplest — make `is_valid_tenant` GUID-only, drop the domain wording from config.rs:43 and config_screen.rs:125/176, and add a unit test in service/mod.rs asserting the tid check; or (b) keep domain support by resolving it once at `AppState::new` (GET `{login_authority_root}/{domain}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration`, take the GUID from `issuer`) and comparing `tid` against the resolved GUID, persisting the GUID back to settings.json so `remembered_account_for` matches. Either way add a test with a domain-form `tenant_id` so the contract is pinned.

findings.rationale: The minisign key that authorizes silent code delivery to every installed copy is readable by every `build.rs` and proc-macro in the ~600-crate dependency graph during the compile phase, because the CLI only needs it after cargo finishes. A single compromised transitive crate exfiltrating `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` from the release runner defeats the whole signed-update model that the pubkey guard, SHA-pinned actions and deny.toml exist to protect. Restoring `rust-cache` into the release job additionally lets cached compiled artifacts from CI runs feed the shipped binary. The repo already has the exact post-build signing step needed (line 176-180) for one platform.
findings.proposal: Split the release recipe into a compile phase without the key and a sign phase with it: `cargo tauri build --no-bundle` (no signing env) then `cargo tauri bundle --config updater-build.json` with the two env vars scoped to that step only (tauri-cli 2.x supports `bundle` on a prebuilt binary); or keep one build and run `cargo tauri signer sign` over each updater artifact in a dedicated step as the NSIS refresh already does. Drop `Swatinem/rust-cache` from the release job (or set `save-if: false` and `lookup-only`) so tag builds compile from source. Document the contract in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md release section.

.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28:
- **CSP governs the *webview*, not backend egress.** `connect-src` in `tauri.conf.json` restricts only WASM frontend fetches; backend reqwest calls to new hosts need no CSP change.
findings.rationale: Every network call goes through backend reqwest via IPC; the frontend has no fetch binding at all (grep for fetch/Request/XmlHttpRequest/WebSocket in web-rs/src finds only unrelated words). The list is therefore dead permission that the repo's own rules say should not exist. It is not harmless: `https://*.vault.azure.net` lets any webview-side script bug exfiltrate data to an attacker-owned Key Vault hostname (Key Vault diagnostic logs record the request URI even for 401s), and the login/graph hosts give the same script a way to make authenticated-looking requests with the operator's browser cookies. Tauri appends its own IPC origins to connect-src at runtime, so `'self'` is sufficient.
findings.proposal: Reduce to `connect-src 'self'` (verify under `just dev` that IPC and the updater still work — the updater runs in the backend), keep `img-src 'self' data:` and the existing script-src. Add a `repo_invariants` test that parses tauri.conf.json and asserts connect-src contains no `https://` origin unless a matching frontend fetch exists, and update the CSP gotcha in AGENTS.md / .claude/rules to say the list is intentionally empty of remote origins.

findings.title: SAML/OIDC summary URLs and the federation-metadata probe hard-code the commercial login host, ignoring CloudEnvironment
findings.rationale: The app advertises sovereign-cloud support (`AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD`, per-cloud Graph/Exchange/KV/ARM/Log Analytics hosts, a `cloud` field in backups that refuses cross-cloud restores), yet the SSO tab's copy-paste 'Login URL / Logout URL / Metadata URL' and the OIDC authority/discovery URL (`oidc_summary_urls`, line 100) are commercial-only. Microsoft Learn (authentication-national-cloud) confirms Gov and China use `login.microsoftonline.us` / `login.partner.microsoftonline.cn`. In a GCC-High tenant an operator configuring a service provider from these values gets a broken IdP, and `probe_federation_metadata` fetches the wrong host so every staged rollover reads as 'couldn't check'. `app_id` is also interpolated into the query unvalidated (no `is_guid` call anywhere in sso/mod.rs).
findings.proposal: Thread `state.auth.cloud()` into `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` and use `login_authority_root()`; add `CloudEnvironment::saml_issuer_root()` (commercial/Gov `https://sts.windows.net`, China `https://sts.chinacloudapi.cn`) next to the other per-cloud getters; validate `app_id` with `guid::is_guid` before building the metadata URL. Add a test asserting the Gov cloud yields `login.microsoftonline.us` URLs.

findings.title: `TokenResponse` derives Debug with plaintext access, refresh and id tokens — the one secret-bearing type without a redacted Debug
findings.rationale: No call site Debug-prints it today (grep for `?token`/`{token:?}` in the auth crate is empty), so this is latent — but the repo has explicitly elevated 'derived Debug on a secret' to a defect class and hand-wrote Debug for AccessToken, PasswordCredential, SecretValue, SecretSetRequest, GeneratedCert(ificateResult), RegeneratedSecret and KvSecretValueDto. The refresh token is the most valuable secret the process ever holds and this struct is the only type that carries it in plaintext; one future `tracing::debug!(?token, ...)` while debugging AAD responses writes it to the 14-day rolling log.
findings.proposal: Replace the derive with a hand-written `Debug` that prints `<redacted>` for the three token fields (keep `expires_in`/`scope`), and add a test mirroring `a_generated_private_key_and_pfx_are_redacted_in_debug`. Optionally add a repo-invariant test that greps for `derive(...Debug...)` on structs with fields named `*_token`/`secret*`/`*password*`.

findings.title: Loopback listener aborts the whole sign-in on a foreign `state` or `error` query from any local process, and serves the success page before validating
findings.rationale: The listener already loops past favicon/preconnect noise, but a request carrying `?error=x` or `?code=x&state=forged` — which any unprivileged local process can send to the ephemeral port during the 300 s window — terminates the flow, so the real redirect that arrives moments later is lost and the operator sees 'state mismatch — possible CSRF' or the raw attacker-chosen `error` string in the toast. RFC 8252 loopback guidance is to ignore requests that do not match the outstanding state. The 200 'sign-in complete' page is also written before the state check, so a forged request gets a success page.
findings.proposal: Check `state == expected_state` first; on mismatch (or when `error` arrives without a matching state) answer `400 Bad Request` and `continue` the accept loop instead of returning. Only after the state matches, branch on `error` vs `code` and write the success/failure page. Constrain the surfaced `error` to the OAuth error-code alphabet (`[a-z_]+`) before it reaches `AuthError::Authorization`. Extend `state_mismatch_is_rejected` to assert the listener still delivers the genuine redirect afterwards.

findings.title: Graph/ARM/Key Vault error bodies flow raw and uncapped into errors, logs and the UI, unlike the Exchange client's sanitized bodies
findings.rationale: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md 'Token & secret security model' says response bodies are 'control-char-stripped and length-capped ... never a raw body that could carry token material', but only the Exchange client does this. The Graph, ARM and Key Vault clients put the full body into `Forbidden/NotFound/Api/Server`, which `?err` logs write to disk verbatim (audit.rs:1497, consent.rs:187/200, keyvault_rbac.rs:120/192, managed_identity.rs:238, keyvault.rs) and `UiError::from` shows in toasts. A proxy/WAF block page (the case post_token explicitly guards against) or a multi-MB HTML error lands unbounded in the 14-day log.
findings.proposal: Move `sanitize_error_body` into `azapptoolkit-core` (next to `http_retry`/`http_error`) and call it at the four body-capture sites (graph transport.rs:597, arm/transport.rs, keyvault client.rs `let body_text = resp.text()...`, exchange keeps its own call). Add a shared unit test and update DEVELOPMENT.md to name the core helper.

findings.title: Log directory is created with the process umask while every other artifact is owner-only
findings.rationale: The rolling logs carry tenant ids, the signed-in scope set, authorize endpoint, app display names (audit.rs:1497), correlation ids, Graph error bodies (see previous finding) and panic backtraces, and settings.json was made 0600 for a weaker class of content ('config-sensitive'). `tracing_appender` creates files with default 0644 under whatever mode `create_dir_all` gives the directory, so on a shared Linux/macOS workstation with a 755 home the 14 days of logs are world-readable.
findings.proposal: On unix create the directory with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` (std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt) and, after `create_dir_all`, `set_permissions(0o700)` so an existing directory is tightened too; document the Windows ACL inheritance the same way `private_file` does. One-line note in DEVELOPMENT.md's security model.

findings.title: Webview capability grants `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` that no frontend code invokes
findings.evidence:
capabilities/default.json:6-12:
  "permissions": [
    "core:default",
    "core:window:default",
    "core:app:default",
    "updater:default",
    "dialog:allow-save"
  ]

commands/updater.rs:26-27 (backend drives the plugin, needs no capability):
pub async fn check_for_update(app: AppHandle) -> Result<Option<UpdateInfo>, UiError> {
    let updater = app.updater().map_err(updater_err)?;

commands/export.rs:86-91:
        let chosen = app_handle
            .dialog()
            .file()
            .add_filter(filter_name, &[ext])
findings.rationale: Capabilities gate what the webview may `invoke` on plugins. Grep of web-rs/src for `plugin:` finds only the mock bridge's `plugin:event|*` routes; every save/open dialog and every update check/download goes through a `#[tauri::command]` in the backend, which uses `AppHandle` APIs that are not capability-gated. `updater:default` in particular lets webview-side code call `plugin:updater|download_and_install` directly — the silent-install path AGENTS.md says must never be reintroduced — so a compromised webview could bypass the interactive splash. Least privilege says grant only what the frontend uses.
findings.proposal: Remove `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` from capabilities/default.json, run `just dev` and exercise an export, backup load, and update check to confirm nothing regresses; add a `repo_invariants` test asserting the capability file lists only `core:*` permissions unless `web-rs/src` contains a matching `plugin:<name>|` invoke.

findings.title: Release-note markdown links render any `href` scheme, and the update splash feeds it the unsigned `latest.json` `notes` field
findings.rationale: The minisign signature covers the downloaded bundle, not `latest.json`; its `notes` field is trusted only via TLS to github.com. Anyone who can edit the release asset (repo/CI compromise without the signing key) can therefore inject `[Update](javascript:...)` or a custom-scheme link that renders as a clickable anchor inside the privileged webview. Today `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks `javascript:` navigation, so this is defense in depth rather than an exploitable hole — but it is the only remote-content-to-DOM path in the app and a one-line allowlist closes it independently of CSP.
findings.proposal: In `parse_link` (or `render_inline`) accept only `https://` (optionally `http://`) hrefs and render anything else as plain text; add a unit test with `javascript:` and `file:` inputs next to the existing `parse_inline` tests. Mention in release-updater-demo.md that `notes` is unsigned content.

findings.title: Log Analytics `workspace_customer_id` from an ARM response is interpolated into the request path unvalidated, unlike the sibling `get_role_definition` guard
findings.rationale: `usage.rs::discover_workspace` passes `properties.customerId` straight from `list_log_analytics_workspaces` into this path with the Log Analytics bearer attached. The ARM client's own doc comment classifies values echoed from ARM responses as attacker-influenced and validates them structurally before composing a URL; this second consumer of the same class has no check, so a value containing `/`, `?`, `#` or `..` reshapes the request (`?` would let a second query override `timespan`, `..` walks the path). The host is fixed so this is not SSRF, but it is an inconsistency in a documented invariant and a GUID check costs one line.
findings.proposal: Reject `workspace_customer_id` that is not a canonical GUID (reuse the shape check from `commands/guid.rs::is_guid`, or add a tiny `is_guid` to core so both crates share it) and return `ArmError::Protocol`, mirroring `get_role_definition`'s error text; add a wiremock test that a `../x?y` id is refused before any request is sent.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:54-55 — `sign_out` drops `graph_clients`/`exchange_clients` but leaves `kv_clients`, `arm_clients`, `la_clients` for the tenant; harmless (adapters re-resolve via `known_tenants`) but inconsistent with the 'sweep everything tenant-scoped' comment beside it.

result.area_summary: Dependency hygiene is deliberate and well-argued where it matters: the crypto holds (no rsa, p12-keystore 0.2.x, transitive-only sha2) are still valid against today's registry (cms max is still 0.3.0-pre.2, p12-keystore 0.3.2 rides it), the two advisory ignore lists are in sync and pinned by a test, the RUSTSEC-2024-0429 drop condition is not met (glib locked at 0.18.5, fix needs 0.20), every license expression in both trees falls inside deny.toml's allow list, no dependency's rust_version exceeds MSRV 1.98 (web-rs max is 1.88), both lockfiles are current to within one zerocopy patch, and every duplicate major in `cargo tree -d` is transitive and platform-bound (GTK3/glib on Linux, swift-rs on macOS, schemars/system-deps at build time, oauth2's rand 0.8) with nothing unifiable from a direct bump. The weak spots are the opposite of the documented ones: six declared-but-unused dependencies (anyhow, thiserror in src-tauri; tracing in keyvault, arm and web-rs) with no tooling gate to catch them, a `[workspace.dependencies]` alias for keyring-core that names a package cargo cannot resolve, system-proxy support for every Graph/Exchange call riding on tauri-plugin-updater's default features rather than our own reqwest declaration, and a tauri-sys git pin (May 2026) that predates upstream's September 2026 workaround for a WASM function-table exhaustion crash in exactly the event-deserialization path this app's eight progress streams use.

findings.title: tauri-sys git pin predates upstream fix for WASM function-table exhaustion in event deserialization
findings.evidence:
apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:31-33:
# Pinned to an exact rev (not the `v2` branch) so WASM builds are reproducible —
# a branch pin silently absorbs whatever upstream pushes. Bump deliberately.
tauri-sys = { git = "https://github.com/JonasKruckenberg/tauri-sys", rev = "289bd29fcbce1ee86c45089477898dbdf23f8fca", features = ["core", "event"] }

Pinned rev source (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tauri-sys-*/289bd29/src/core.rs:126):
    let _ = tx.unbounded_send(serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap());
(same at core.rs:14 `swb::from_value(value).unwrap()` and :25-26 for every invoke result/error)

Upstream v2 branch (fetched): 289bd29 dated 2026-05-08; 4 newer commits incl. 1ffc6fa 2026-09-08 "Update conversion of `JsValues` (#113)" whose PR text says it addresses wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen#5324 and bumps to 0.2.5. Issue #5324 title: "WASM function table exhaustion with repeated `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value()` in closures" — "A Tauri + Leptos application crashes with 'RuntimeError: Out of bounds table access' after deserializing multiple events".

Our consumption: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/events.rs:19 `listen::<AuditProgress>("audit-progress")` (8 such streams: audit, bulk, backup, restore, site-sweep, keyvault-sweep, mailbox-probe, updater); backend has 30 `.emit(` sites, e.g. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:993 `progress.emit(BulkProgress {`. crates.io: "crate `tauri-sys` does not exist" — git is the only channel, and dependabot.yml:72-83 cannot advance a git rev.
findings.rationale: The reported failure mode (Tauri + Leptos, many events deserialized through serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value inside the listener closure) is exactly this app's progress-stream path, and a tenant-wide audit or bulk remediation emits one event per app across thousands of apps. Upstream shipped a workaround four commits after the pinned rev; the pin comment says "bump deliberately" but there is no crates.io release for Dependabot to track and no reminder mechanism, so the pin silently rots. Not reproduced in this repo — probability scales with event volume — but a webview crash mid-bulk-run is severe and the fix is upstream already.
findings.proposal: Bump the rev to 1ffc6fa (or the v2 head 571cef4) in apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml, regenerate apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.lock, and adapt apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/ to any error.rs/event.rs API change (the bindings module already isolates tauri-sys, so blast radius is small; `just web-itest` is the gate). Then record the review date next to the pin and add a lightweight freshness check (a `just deps-git-status` recipe that runs `git ls-remote` against the allowed git source and prints commits ahead of the pinned rev, or a quarterly CHANGELOG/AGENTS reminder), since neither Dependabot nor cargo-audit covers git revs.

Cargo.toml:43:
keyring-core = { package = "keyring_core", version = "1.0" }

crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:20 (the only consumer, NOT via workspace):
keyring-core = "1.0"

Cargo.lock:2655-2657:
name = "keyring-core"
version = "1.0.0"

The moment anyone follows AGENTS.md's rule and switches auth to `keyring-core = { workspace = true }`, resolution fails with a confusing error. It also breaks the workspace's own convention that shared deps are workspace-managed.

findings.title: System-proxy support for all Graph/Exchange/KeyVault/ARM traffic depends on tauri-plugin-updater's default features, not our reqwest declaration
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:29:
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json", "query", "form"] }

reqwest-0.13.5/Cargo.toml [features]:
default = ["default-tls", "charset", "http2", "system-proxy"]
system-proxy = ["hyper-util/client-proxy-system"]

`cargo tree --locked -p desktop -e features -i reqwest`:
└── reqwest feature "system-proxy"
    └── tauri-plugin-updater feature "system-proxy"
        └── tauri-plugin-updater feature "default"

tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0/Cargo.toml:
default = ["rustls-tls", "system-proxy", "zip"]

No proxy configuration anywhere in our code (grep -i proxy over crates/*/src and src-tauri/src finds only comments about proxies answering with text/html).
findings.rationale: Corporate Entra admins commonly sit behind a proxy configured in Windows Internet Settings or macOS System Configuration (not env vars). Today the shipped binary honours those settings only because the updater plugin happens to enable reqwest's `system-proxy` and features unify. Trimming the updater's defaults (e.g. to drop `zip`), a plugin default change, or a build variant without the updater would silently make every Graph call fail behind such proxies — and no test or comment records that this feature is load-bearing for the app's own clients.
findings.proposal: Add "system-proxy" to the workspace reqwest feature list in Cargo.toml:29 with a one-line comment ("OS proxy discovery for corporate Windows/macOS deployments; enabled here on purpose, not inherited from the updater plugin"). Zero cost today (already unified in); it makes the dependency explicit and survives any updater-plugin change. Optionally add a repo_invariants test that greps the feature in Cargo.toml.

findings.title: src-tauri declares anyhow and thiserror but uses neither; anyhow is then unused workspace-wide

apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43:
anyhow = { workspace = true }
thiserror = { workspace = true }

`grep -rn 'anyhow\|thiserror' apps/desktop/src-tauri/src apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs` → no output.

anyhow = "1"
(`cargo tree -i anyhow` shows `desktop` as the only workspace consumer; every other edge is tauri/tauri-build/tauri-utils.)

findings.title: tracing declared but never used in azapptoolkit-keyvault, azapptoolkit-arm and web-rs
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20:
tracing = { workspace = true }
crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19:
tracing = { workspace = true }

For web-rs remove it, or if browser-side tracing is wanted, add `tracing-wasm`/console subscriber deliberately and document it in frontend-workspace.md.

findings.title: No unused-dependency gate in verify-full/CI; six dead declarations slipped through
findings.evidence:
justfile:354-355:
deny:
    cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources
justfile:334-335:
audit:
    cargo audit

`grep -n -i 'udeps\|machete\|shear\|outdated' justfile .github/workflows/ci.yml` → no matches.

Dead declarations found by hand in this review: anyhow + thiserror (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43), tracing (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20, crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19, apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63).
findings.rationale: The repo gates advisories, licenses, sources, yanked crates and even the sync of two ignore lists, yet nothing checks that a declared dependency is used. cargo-machete is stable-toolchain, sub-second, and needs no build, so it fits `verify-full` and the existing `deny` CI job without touching the compile matrix.
findings.proposal: Add a `just udeps` recipe running `cargo machete --with-metadata` over the root and `apps/desktop/web-rs`, wire it into `verify-full` and the `deny` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (pin the tool version like cargo-deny@0.20.2 is). Add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to graph/arm/keyvault only if the http_error_enum! re-export refactor (separate finding) is not taken.

findings.title: http_error_enum! expands to ::thiserror::Error, forcing a phantom thiserror dependency on every caller
findings.rationale: Macro hygiene convention is `$crate::__private::dep` so the defining crate owns the dependency. Here the crate that owns the taxonomy does not declare thiserror while three callers must — and their manifests give no hint why (a grep of their src shows nothing using it). Any unused-dependency cleanup (manual or via cargo-machete, which this review recommends) removes those lines and the build fails inside a macro expansion with a confusing `::thiserror` path error.
findings.proposal: Add `thiserror = { workspace = true }` to crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml, add `#[doc(hidden)] pub use thiserror;` in core's lib.rs, change line 65 to `#[derive(Debug, $crate::thiserror::Error)]`, and drop the now-redundant thiserror lines from graph/arm/keyvault. Lockfile unchanged.

findings.title: time dependency is undocumented and leaks across the cert.rs boundary into a chrono-only codebase
findings.rationale: `time` is genuinely required: rcgen 0.14's `CertificateParams.not_before/not_after` are `time::OffsetDateTime`. But the manifest gives no hint, so the next reviewer asks the same "two time crates?" question, and `GeneratedCert` exposes `time::OffsetDateTime` publicly, pushing the second date library (and a manual unix-timestamp round-trip) into a command layer that otherwise uses chrono exclusively.
findings.proposal: Add a one-line comment at Cargo.toml:88 ("rcgen's validity fields are time::OffsetDateTime; chrono everywhere else"), and convert inside cert.rs so `GeneratedCert.not_after` is `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` — making `time` a private detail of the one module that needs it and removing the conversion at credentials.rs:140-141.

findings.title: parking_lot and std::sync locks are mixed with no rule, and the std sites exist only to recover from poisoning parking_lot doesn't have
findings.rationale: Same file (token_cache.rs) uses parking_lot::RwLock at line 11 and std::sync::Mutex at line 239. The two std sites each carry a paragraph explaining poison recovery via `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` — behaviour that parking_lot gives for free (no poisoning, const `new`). Either the codebase wants poisoning semantics (then the parking_lot sites silently lack them) or it doesn't (then the std sites are extra code plus prose).
findings.proposal: Pick one and write it down in AGENTS.md Coding fundamentals: given parking_lot is already a workspace dep and in the graph via tao, use `parking_lot::Mutex`/`RwLock` at the four std sites (dropping the poison-recovery closures and their comments), or the reverse if poisoning is wanted. Either way it is a mechanical change with no lockfile impact.

findings.title: Workspace tokio feature set is the union; every library crate inherits net/io-util/rt-multi-thread/macros it doesn't use
findings.rationale: Feature unification means the shipped binary is unaffected, so this is precision, not size: the manifests claim every client crate needs a multi-thread runtime and raw TCP, which is false and hides that the OAuth loopback listener is the single place raw sockets are opened — a fact worth being visible in a credential tool. It also slightly inflates `just test-crate <lib>` builds.
findings.proposal: Set the workspace entry to the common core (`features = ["sync", "time"]`), add `features = ["net", "io-util"]` in crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml with a comment naming loopback.rs, and `features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"]` in apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml (dev-dependencies already add `macros`/`rt` where tests need them).

apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:38: futures = { workspace = true }

findings.title: reqwest http2 is off, so every Graph/Exchange fan-out multiplexes over HTTP/1.1 connections
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:29:
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json", "query", "form"] }

reqwest-0.13.5 default = ["default-tls", "charset", "http2", "system-proxy"] — `http2` is dropped by default-features = false and nothing re-enables it:
`cargo tree --locked -p desktop -e features -i reqwest` lists: __rustls, __rustls-aws-lc-rs, __tls, form, json, query, rustls, rustls-no-provider, stream, system-proxy (no http2).
`cargo tree -i h2 --target all` → "nothing to print" (h2 is not in the graph on any target).
findings.rationale: Graph, Exchange Admin and Key Vault endpoints negotiate h2 via ALPN. With HTTP/1.1 only, a `ConcurrencyThrottle` fan-out at N in-flight requests holds N TLS connections per host; with h2 it multiplexes streams over one connection, cutting handshakes and connection-pool churn behind corporate proxies. Benefit is unmeasured here and `$batch` already reduces request count, so this is a measure-first item, not a defect.
findings.proposal: Add `"http2"` to the workspace reqwest features (adds the `h2` crate), run an existing fan-out (e.g. the site sweep or audit on a large tenant) with `RUST_LOG=hyper_util=debug` before/after to count connections and wall time, keep it if it wins. Record the result next to the opt-level bench in Cargo.toml so it is not re-asked.

result.coverage_notes: Read fully: Cargo.toml (root), apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml, apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml, all eight crates/*/Cargo.toml, deny.toml, .cargo/audit.toml, .github/dependabot.yml, rust-toolchain.toml, apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/dependency_policy.rs, the crypto-pins section of docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md, and the justfile/ci.yml audit+deny recipes. Cargo.lock (6891 lines) and apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.lock (2560 lines) were not read line by line; they were interrogated via `cargo tree --locked` (-d, -i, -e features, --target all), `cargo metadata --locked` (license and rust_version surveys on both trees), `cargo update --dry-run` (no files written; git status confirmed both lockfiles untouched), and targeted greps. Per the rules I did not run cargo build/test/clippy/check, cargo deny or cargo audit — license coverage and advisory sync were checked by hand against cargo metadata and the two ignore lists. Network: crates.io API and the tauri-sys GitHub pages (commits/v2, PR #113, wasm-bindgen issue #5324) were reachable via WebFetch; the raw commit diff for upstream 1ffc6fa was NOT retrievable (GitHub REST via the proxy returned an access notice and the GitHub MCP tool is scoped to tiredithumans/azapptoolkit), so the tauri-sys finding relies on the pinned rev's source in ~/.cargo/git/checkouts, the upstream commit message/PR text, and the issue text rather than the fix's exact after-state. Dependency-usage scan was a regex over `name::`, `name!`, and derive paths across src/, tests/, build.rs of each crate, followed by plain-text greps for every zero-hit result.

result.area_summary: The API surface is in good shape: every Graph call uses v1.0 except the sign-in-activity report, which is still beta-only per Learn (no v1.0 exists), ARM authorization uses the current stable 2022-04-01, Log Analytics uses the current v1 endpoint, the RBAC-for-Applications cmdlets and the Sites.Selected/grantedToV2 bodies match the docs, and composite Exchange roles and nested-group limits are handled. The weak spots are (a) the scoping/audit role map deliberately stops at the AAP-era permission set, so newer RBAC-scopable Graph mailbox permissions (MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.*) are invisible to the mailbox advisory and un-scopable in the wizard; (b) two on-demand tokens (group membership, claims-mapping) are minted with a single scope where Learn documents a required pair, and two on-demand features have no capabilities-catalog entry; (c) the SSO wizard hardcodes global-cloud identifiers although the code base otherwise models sovereign clouds; (d) the Exchange transport rides an undocumented gateway that the repo's comments and doc links present as the documented Admin API; and several ARM/Key Vault api-versions are behind current stable.

findings.title: Mailbox advisory and scope map miss the newer RBAC-scopable Graph mailbox permissions (MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.*, MailboxConfigItem.*)
findings.rationale: The comment justifies the 10-entry map by the AAP migration ("never AAP-scopable"), but the same map is the gate for every non-AAP path: `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:126-131) decides whether the Grant-access wizard and the Scope fix offer confinement, and `is_mailbox_reaching_permission` decides membership in the audit's mailbox advisory. `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` (read/write/delete every item in every mailbox) and `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All` (common in third-party backup apps) do not start with `Mail.`, so an org-wide grant of them produces no mailbox finding, no high-risk points, and no Scope action, even though Exchange documents a scoped role for each. That is the direction a least-privilege audit must not be wrong in. The name-shaped fallback's own doc comment claims it catches permissions "this build's graph_mail_role table doesn't know yet" but the prefix list cannot match `Mailbox`- or `Mail-`-prefixed names.
findings.proposal: Extend `graph_mail_role` with the 14 additional documented roles (MailboxFolder.Read/ReadWrite.All, MailboxItem.Read/ReadWrite/Export/ImportExport.All, MailboxConfigItem.Read/ReadWrite, MailTips.ReadBasic.All, Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All, SMTP.SendAsApp) with a table-driven test citing the Learn table; keep a separate, smaller `AAP_SCOPABLE` set for `aap.rs` if the migration path must stay conservative. Widen `mailbox_named` to `Mailbox`/`Mail-` prefixes. Add `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All` to `HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS` (and the read variants to medium), with the CHANGELOG note AGENTS.md requires for a ranking shift. Expected effect: backup/archival apps holding org-wide item-level permissions appear in the mailbox advisory and can be scoped.

findings.title: SSO wizard hardcodes the global-cloud application template id and login host; sovereign clouds fail
findings.rationale: The rest of the backend resolves Graph, Exchange, ARM, Key Vault and Log Analytics hosts through `CloudEnvironment`, so the product advertises sovereign-cloud support, yet the SSO wizard's `POST /applicationTemplates/{id}/instantiate` will 404 in US Gov and China (wrong template GUID) and the SAML/OIDC URLs handed to app owners point at the commercial login host.
findings.proposal: Add `CloudEnvironment::custom_app_template_id() -> &'static str` returning the three documented GUIDs (DoD shares the US Gov id), replace `CUSTOM_TEMPLATE_ID` with `state.auth.cloud().custom_app_template_id()` at mod.rs:167/313, and replace `LOGIN_HOST` with `state.auth.cloud().login_authority_root()` at mod.rs:90-100. Add a unit test in cloud.rs pinning the three ids.

findings.title: Group-membership token requests only GroupMember.ReadWrite.All; Learn documents that adding a servicePrincipal member also requires Application.ReadWrite.All
findings.rationale: The member the app always adds is a service principal, which is exactly the row the docs single out. The dedicated token is minted from a single-scope request, so whether the resulting `scp` also carries `Application.ReadWrite.All` depends on the tenant having previously consented the write bundle for this client, not on anything the code asserts. The readiness checklist probes `consent_scopes_for("group_membership")` and reports the scope half as satisfied with only GroupMember consented, while the POST can still be rejected. Because outcomes vary with consent history, this is a latent 403 that the catalog cannot explain.
findings.proposal: Change `default_graph_group_member_scopes` to `graph_scopes(&["GroupMember.ReadWrite.All", "Application.ReadWrite.All"])`, list both in the `group_membership` capability `scopes`, and mention the pair in its remediation string. Add a scopes.rs test mirroring `write_scopes_cover_mutations`.

findings.title: Claims-mapping policy assign/list ride a Policy-only token; Learn requires Application.ReadWrite.All AND a Policy.* scope
findings.rationale: Creating the policy (`POST /policies/claimsMappingPolicies`) genuinely needs only `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration`, but the two `$ref` operations on the service principal are documented as needing `Application.ReadWrite.All` in the same token. As with the group-member token, success today depends on Entra folding previously consented write scopes into a single-scope request. Listing assigned policies is also a read that could ride `Policy.Read.All` + `Application.ReadWrite.All` rather than forcing the admin-consent-only write scope on a read path.
findings.proposal: Mint the policy-write token with `["Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration", "Application.ReadWrite.All"]`; consider routing `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` through the existing `policy_token` (Policy.Read.All) plus the write bundle so a browse-only SSO view never requests the write scope. Document the pair in a new capability entry (see the catalog-gap finding).

findings.title: Capabilities catalog has no entry for the `policy_write` (claims mapping) and `sync` (provisioning) on-demand scopes
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:1-2: "Authorization-capability catalog: the single source of truth mapping each privileged feature area to the role(s) and delegated OAuth scope(s) it needs."
CAPABILITIES (lines 125-404) `scope_feature` values: "write", "audit_log", "policy", "sharepoint", "group_membership", "keyvault", "arm", "log_analytics", "exchange" — no entry with Some("policy_write") or Some("sync").
state.rs:534-543:
    pub fn consent_scopes_for(&self, feature: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
            "sync" => self.auth.default_graph_sync_scopes(),
            "policy_write" => self.auth.default_graph_policy_write_scopes(),

Microsoft Learn, List synchronization jobs (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/synchronization-synchronization-list-jobs?view=graph-rest-1.0): least privileged delegated `Synchronization.Read.All`; supported roles "Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator".
findings.rationale: Both features are admin-consent-only and role-gated, so a 403 on the provisioning tab or on SAML claim customization has no `forbidden_remediation` hint, no `RequiresRole` label, and no readiness row — exactly the drift the catalog header says it exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Add two `Capability` rows: `saml_claims_mapping` (Plane::EntraDirectory; roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / Global Administrator; scopes per the claims-mapping finding; scope_feature Some("policy_write")) and `provisioning_status` (roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / Hybrid Identity Administrator with template ids; scopes ["Synchronization.Read.All"]; scope_feature Some("sync")). Add a test asserting every `consent_scopes_for` key except "write" has a catalog row, and splice `forbidden_remediation` into the SSO claims and provisioning commands.

findings.title: Exchange client rides the undocumented `adminapi/beta/{tenant}/InvokeCommand` gateway while comments and doc links present it as the documented Admin API
findings.rationale: The route the app depends on for every scoping mutation is the ExchangeOnlineManagement module's private transport, not the documented (preview) REST surface, and the documented surface does not expose any RBAC-for-Applications cmdlet. That is a legitimate engineering choice, but the repo currently (a) carries a pre-launch "verify during the live transport spike" note on production code, (b) cites the v2.0 get-started page as the contract for an endpoint that page does not describe, and (c) nowhere records the support risk or the trigger for migrating (RBAC cmdlets appearing under `adminapi/v2.0`).
findings.proposal: Replace the stale NOTE with a paragraph stating that `InvokeCommand` is the EXO PowerShell module's transport (unsupported for third parties), that the documented Admin API is `adminapi/v2.0/{tenant}/{Endpoint}` with `Exchange.ManageV2` and today covers none of the cmdlets in `rbac.rs`, and name the watch condition. Add the same note to docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md. Keep the pagination link but scope its wording to "the same nextLink/POST-continuation contract the documented API uses".

findings.title: ARM and Key Vault api-versions are behind current stable releases (Key Vault data plane moved to date-based versions; a control-plane retirement is in progress)
findings.rationale: AUTHORIZATION_API and SUBSCRIPTIONS_API are current. KEYVAULT_API (control plane) is three stable releases behind and Microsoft has an active control-plane API-version retirement for Key Vault; LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACES_API is four behind; the data-plane 7.4 predates the switch to date-based versions. Old versions keep working until retired, but the retirement page is the signal that this cannot stay unreviewed indefinitely, and the constants carry no review date or source link.
findings.proposal: Bump KEYVAULT_API to 2024-11-01 (or later stable), LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACES_API to 2023-09-01 or 2025-02-01, and DEFAULT_API_VERSION to 2025-07-01 after checking the retirement list on the migrate-api-version page; add a `// Source: <url>, reviewed YYYY-MM` comment per constant so the next reviewer can diff quickly. The wiremock tests already assert `query_param("api-version", CONST)` so they follow automatically.

findings.title: Readiness checklist cannot recognise the custom Entra role the repo itself recommends
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:428-451 `matched_directory_role` matches only `role_template_id` against the built-in TID_* constants or the catalog display names:
    for role in active_roles {
        if let Some(tid) = role.role_template_id.as_deref()
            && let Some((name, _)) = cap.directory_roles_any.iter()
                .find(|(_, want)| want.is_some_and(|w| w.eq_ignore_ascii_case(tid)))
directory.rs:116-123 reads `/me/transitiveMemberOf/microsoft.graph.directoryRole`.
docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md:19: "So: **two custom roles + one built-in role**." and ships `entra-custom-role.ps1`; grep of that file for "checklist|readiness|detect" returns nothing.

Microsoft Learn, List Microsoft Entra role assignments (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/view-assignments#list-microsoft-entra-role-assignments): "GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments?$filter=principalId+eq+'<object-id-of-principal>'" and "List role assignments with app registration scope ... $filter=directoryScopeId+eq+'/<app object id>'".
findings.rationale: An operator following OPERATOR-ROLES.md holds a custom role whose template id is tenant-specific, so every DirectoryRole-detected capability reads "Role missing" for them; the doc does not warn about this. The unified RBAC API can return the operator's role assignments with their definitions (`allowedResourceActions`), which is what the catalog actually cares about, and it also exposes app-scoped assignments (`directoryScopeId eq '/<appObjectId>'`) that neither the checklist nor the app detail (owners only) shows today.
findings.proposal: Add an optional `required_actions: &[&str]` per capability (e.g. `microsoft.directory/applications/credentials/update`) and a second detection path via `roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments?$filter=principalId eq '{me}'&$expand=roleDefinition` (RoleManagement.Read.Directory, or fall back to the existing directoryRole read); report a custom role whose actions cover the set as "have (custom role X)". Separately, surface app-scoped role assignments on the app detail next to Owners. Document the current limitation in OPERATOR-ROLES.md in the meantime.

findings.title: Adopt appCredentialSignInActivities (same AuditLog.Read.All token) for per-credential last-used and an unused-credential finding
findings.rationale: The app already pays for the token, roles, and licence this report needs and already caches the sibling SP report per tenant. Per-key last-used lets the credential dashboard and the audit distinguish a live secret from a stale one, turns the "remove expired credentials" fix into a safe "remove never-used / long-unused credentials" fix, and tells rotation flows which of two overlapping secrets is still in use before revoking. Beta-only and Global-cloud-only, so it must degrade like the SP report.
findings.proposal: Add `list_app_credential_sign_in_activities()` next to the SP report (same beta_base, same cache bucket with its own key, same MAX_PAGES/origin guards), join on `keyId` into the credential DTOs, add an audit rule "credential unused for N days" gated on `sign_in_report_available`, and surface last-used in the Credentials tab. Note national-cloud unavailability in the capability description.

findings.title: Read tenant/app management policies (v1.0) to pre-validate secret lifetimes and explain policy-driven 400s
findings.rationale: Tenants increasingly enable `passwordAddition`/`passwordLifetime` restrictions; today the app discovers them only as an opaque Graph 400 after the operator has chosen a lifetime. The app already has an on-demand `Policy.Read.All` token (`policy_token`, used for Conditional Access), so reading the default policy and any `appManagementPolicies` applied to the app is one extra GET with no new consent. It also gives the audit a tenant-posture signal ("secret creation not blocked tenant-wide").
findings.proposal: Add `get_default_app_management_policy()` and `list_app_management_policies_for(app_id)` on `policy_token` (degrade to None like CA), compute the effective max lifetime / addition block, clamp or warn in the add-secret dialog before the POST, map the Graph policy-violation error code to that explanation, and add an audit posture card when the tenant default is disabled.

findings.title: UI and audit text call Application Access Policies "deprecated"; Microsoft's current wording is "legacy, replaced, deprecation to be announced"
findings.evidence:
groups.rs:63-64:
        title: "Legacy Application Access Policy scoping",
        blurb: "Mailbox access confined by an Application Access Policy — deprecated, per-app, and blind to anything granted through Exchange RBAC. ..."
scope_badge.rs:270: "// Legacy Application Access Policy: genuinely scoped, but deprecated —"
commands/exchange/mod.rs:3: "//! These replace the deprecated Application Access Policy flow"

Microsoft Learn, Application Access Policies (legacy) (https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/application-access-policies): "App Access Policies has been replaced by Role Based Access Control for Applications ... New access configuration should not use Application Access Policies since this feature will have deprecation announced in the future which will require migration."
findings.rationale: There is no announced deprecation or retirement date yet; telling operators the mechanism is deprecated overstates urgency (and a future announcement with a real date will need distinct wording). The architecture doc (exchange-scoping.md) already uses "legacy" consistently; the UI strings drifted.
findings.proposal: Change the operator-facing strings to "legacy (replaced by RBAC for Applications; Microsoft has said deprecation will be announced)" and keep the migrate Fix; add a CHANGELOG line since the audit blurb is user-visible.

findings.title: `admin_consent` capability omits Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator, which Learn lists as supported for non-Graph app-role grants
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:176-198:
        key: "admin_consent",
        directory_roles_any: &[
            ("Privileged Role Administrator", Some(TID_PRIVILEGED_ROLE_ADMIN)),
            ("Global Administrator", Some(TID_GLOBAL_ADMIN)),
        ],
        remediation: "... A custom or Cloud Application Administrator role is not sufficient for sensitive permissions."

Only Microsoft Graph / AAD Graph app roles require PRA.
findings.proposal: Add ("Application Administrator", TID_APPLICATION_ADMIN) and ("Cloud Application Administrator", TID_CLOUD_APPLICATION_ADMIN) to `directory_roles_any`, and reword description/remediation to state the PRA/GA requirement applies to Microsoft Graph (and AAD Graph) app roles specifically; optionally have the consent command splice a resource-aware hint when the target resource is Graph.

findings.title: `ExoRoleAssignment` does not model `RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope`; an AU-scoped assignment reads as org-wide on the assignment path
findings.evidence:
models.rs:36-47:

    #[serde(rename = "Name", default)] pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "Role", default)] pub role: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "RoleAssigneeName", default)] pub role_assignee_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "CustomResourceScope", default)] pub custom_resource_scope: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "Identity", default)] pub identity: Option<String>,
}

Microsoft Learn, RBAC for Applications (https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/application-rbac#configuration-instructions): "New-ManagementRoleAssignment ... -CustomResourceScope <Management Scope> (or -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope)"; Example Two: "New-ManagementRoleAssignment -App ... -Role \"Application Mail.Read\" -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope 4d819ce9-...".

result.area_summary: The product surface is unusually complete for its niche: 200+ commands, a findings-first security workbench with one-click fixes, Exchange RBAC + Sites.Selected scoping, DR backup/restore, reverse lookups and a readiness checklist, all with honest coverage reporting. The two open least-privilege issues are well scoped by the owner (#109 unblocked and designed in detail, #110 correctly walkthrough-gated), and every seam they name exists in the tree. The real gaps sit one step past the current seams: Entra's 30-day soft-delete is neither surfaced nor acknowledged (the delete dialogs say "cannot be undone"), the Conditional Access tab parses only `conditions.applications` and so misses workload-identity CA policies that target the same SP as a client, the ownership rule is skipped for enterprise apps even though SP owners live in this tenant, and tenant app-management policies (the one Entra control that enforces credential lifetime) are absent while the audit hardcodes 365 days. Several header docs still describe restore/credential caching as future or uncached work that has since shipped.

findings.title: Surface Entra's 30-day soft-delete: a 'Recently deleted' list with restore, and fix the 'cannot be undone' delete copy
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #1. Entra soft-deletes application objects for 30 days (`GET /directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.application`, `POST /directory/deletedItems/{id}/restore`, `DELETE /directory/deletedItems/{id}` for permanent removal). The toolkit ships `delete_application` and `bulk_delete_applications` (the latter seeded by multi-select and 'Fix all N' flows) yet has no view of, or route back from, the recycle bin, and both the bulk bar and the CHANGELOG-described single-app dialog tell the operator the action is irreversible. That is the wrong message for the one moment an admin most needs the true one: after a mis-targeted bulk delete they will reach for PowerShell (`Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem`) — exactly what this app exists to replace — or assume the app is gone and recreate it, which mints a new appId and breaks every consumer. The read needs only `Directory.Read.All` (already the sign-in scope); restore/permanent-delete ride the existing `write` scope feature (`Application.ReadWrite.All`). Restoring also re-creates the SP link, so the existing `invalidate_app_lists` + pairing index refresh is the only cache work.
findings.proposal: (1) S: reword the two delete confirmations to state the real semantics — 'Moves the app to Entra's recycle bin; it can be restored for 30 days, after which it is permanently deleted.' (2) M: add `commands/applications/deleted.rs` with `list_deleted_applications` (paged with `$top`, `$select=id,appId,displayName,deletedDateTime`), `restore_deleted_application`, and `purge_deleted_application` (confirm-gated, the only truly irreversible one), register in `generate_handler![]`, add bindings, and a 'Recently deleted' facet or drawer on the App Registrations list (or a Home 'Recently deleted (N)' tile) that deep-links to restore. Bulk delete's completion toast gains a 'Undo (restore N)' action for the session. Add `demo::register_fixtures` entries. Expected effect: bulk delete becomes recoverable inside the tool and the dialogs stop misinforming.

findings.title: Build the file-bridged posture snapshot + drift report (#109) — every seam it names exists and is unblocked
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #2. The owner's 2026-08-04 comment on #109 retired the blocker (backup/export already established the file-bridged, user-initiated persistence posture) and wrote a full design: `PostureSnapshot` = cached `AuditItem`s + `AppPermissionGrantDto`s + coverage + `sign_in_report_available`, a pure `audit::drift::diff`, five commands, a Drift sub-tab. I verified each precondition in the tree: `save_backup_to_file`/`load_backup_from_file` plumbing exists (backup.rs:305-312), `list_app_role_assigned_to` exists (roles_grants.rs:71), `AuditItem` fields are `#[serde(default)]`, and — the two correctness hazards the design calls out — `list_app_permission_grants` really does degrade a failed resource to zero rows (so a naive diff would print 'every Exchange grant removed'), and the finding classifier `matches_finding` really is frontend-only, so the backend diff cannot bucket by stable marker without the §6 move into `azapptoolkit-core::audit`. `AppPermissionGrantDto` still lacks the `resource_app_id` diff key the design requires. Nothing has landed. For an admin this is the difference between 'here is today's posture' and 'here is what changed since the last attestation' — the attestation/trend question is what audit committees actually ask.
findings.proposal: Implement the owner's design as written: (a) additive `resource_app_id: Option<String>` on `AppPermissionGrantDto` and a per-resource `grant_coverage` record emitted by `list_app_permission_grants` in place of the silent `Vec::new()`; (b) move `matches_finding` to `azapptoolkit_core::audit::classify_finding` and have `filter.rs` delegate (keep its characterization tests); (c) `azapptoolkit-dto/src/snapshot.rs` + pure `core::audit::drift::diff` with the fail-closed rules (suppress removals for uncovered resources, omit the unused dimension unless both sides have the report, refuse tenant/cloud mismatch and newer schema, refuse a cancelled run as baseline); (d) `commands/snapshot.rs` with capture/save/load/diff/save-drift riding `export::save_export_via_dialog`; (e) a read-only Drift sub-tab in `SecurityView` (`security_view.rs:74-79`) with the baseline on `TenantScopedUi` + `reset()` line + pinning assertion. findings.title: Conditional Access tab ignores `conditions.clientApplications`, so workload-identity CA policies targeting this service principal are never shown
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #3. Entra has two CA axes for an app: policies whose *target resource* is the app (`conditions.applications.includeApplications`) and Conditional Access for workload identities, where the *subject* is the service principal itself (`conditions.clientApplications.includeServicePrincipals` / `excludeServicePrincipals` / `servicePrincipalFilter`, gated on Workload Identities Premium). The model only deserializes `applications`, and `to_dto` returns `None` when it is absent, so a policy that blocks this SP from untrusted locations, or one that ties it to service-principal risk, renders as 'no policies apply'. For a tool whose subject matter is the service principal (Enterprise Applications, managed identities, the SP-only audit rows), the workload-identity axis is the one an admin hardening app identities cares about — and a tab that says nothing when a block policy exists actively misleads a troubleshooting session ('why does this app get AADSTS53003?'). The candidate list in the task ('Conditional Access for workload identities') is confirmed absent. The fetch already returns whole policy objects with no `$select` (directory.rs:78-95), so this is a model + classifier change with no new Graph call or scope.
findings.proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (include/exclude SP object ids, `servicePrincipalFilter {mode, rule}`) to `CaConditions`; extend `to_dto`/`applies_reason` to take the SP object id as well as the appId and return a distinct reason code (`workloadIdentity`, `workloadIdentityFilter`), with exclude-wins semantics mirrored from the app axis; add a 'Targets' column (resource vs. workload identity) to the CA tab DTO and mount the tab on the Enterprise Application pane too (today it lives only on the app-registration pane per `views/tabs/conditional_access_tab.rs`). Table tests mirroring `all_matches_unless_excluded` for the SP axis. Update README:130. Expected effect: the CA tab answers both 'what protects access to this API' and 'what constrains this identity'.

findings.title: Enterprise-app (SP-only) audit rows skip the ownership rule even though SP owners live in this tenant
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #4. The documented rationale for dropping rules 14-18 on SP-only rows is that the data lives in the home tenant. That is true for credentials and the manifest, but not for owners: `servicePrincipals/{id}/owners` is a local property, the detail pane already reads it (`list_service_principal_owners`), and `add_enterprise_app_owner` (enterprise_application.rs:461) already writes it. Foreign-tenant multi-tenant apps and gallery SaaS apps are precisely the principals that most often end up ownerless in a directory (the consenting admin left; nobody in-tenant is accountable), and they are the rows the audit already scores for org-wide mail/SharePoint reach. Today the 'Missing or single owner' group and the ownerless-app campaign (`bulk_add_owner` → app registrations only) cannot see them. This is an 'ownerless-app campaign' gap the task asked to evaluate; the rationale in the code does not cover the owner axis.

Table tests: foreign SP with 0/1/2 owners; SP rows with owners unresolved (`None`) must not fire. CHANGELOG entry (ranking shifts). Expected effect: ownerless enterprise apps appear in the ownership group and are fixable in bulk.

findings.title: No visibility of tenant app-management policies (credential lifetime / type enforcement) while the audit hardcodes a 365-day 'long-lived' threshold
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #5. Entra's app management policies (`/policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy`, `/policies/appManagementPolicies`, `/applications/{id}/appManagementPolicies`) are the tenant control that *prevents* the findings this audit reports after the fact: `passwordAddition` blocks new client secrets, `passwordLifetime`/`symmetricKeyLifetime` cap durations, `customPasswordAddition` blocks portal-set secrets, `keyCredential` restrictions require asymmetric keys, `nonDefaultUriAddition` blocks URI hijack. The audit's Rules 7 and 17 ('Long-lived secrets (>1 year)', 'Uses client secret(s)') and the per-app Credentials tab give no hint whether the tenant already enforces a policy, whether this app is exempted by a custom policy, or why an `add_password` just failed with a policy violation. The read scope is `Policy.Read.All` (the existing `policy` feature; the same scope already gates the CA tab) and the write scope is `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` (the existing `policy_write` feature used for claims mapping), so no new consent surface is needed. For an admin managing apps at scale this is the difference between remediating each app and turning the tap off once.
findings.proposal: Phase 1 (M, read-only): `GraphClient::get_default_app_management_policy` + `list_app_management_policies` + `list_app_management_policies_for_app` in `policies.rs`; a `TenantAppPolicyDto` folded into `run_audit`'s tenant-wide prefetch (best-effort, degrade to None); (a) Rule 7 compares each secret's lifetime with the effective policy's `passwordLifetime` when present instead of the constant, and adds an advisory 'Tenant does not enforce credential lifetime/type restrictions' finding group with the portal deep-link; (b) a `Callout` on the Credentials tab and in the secret-add dialog naming the effective restrictions so a policy-rejected `add_password` is explained before the click; (c) a Home Security Posture line 'App management policy: enforced / not configured'. Phase 2 (M): `enable_default_app_management_policy` / `assign_app_management_policy` behind `policy_write` with a diff preview, mirroring the claims-mapping write path. Add a `capabilities.rs` entry (`app_management_policy`) so 403s carry the role hint (Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator).

findings.title: Readiness reports a PIM-eligible role as 'Missing' with no way to tell it from 'not assigned', and no activation link
findings.rationale: The checklist deliberately treats an eligible-but-inactive role as absent (documented, and correct as a nudge). But 'Missing' currently conflates two states with different remedies: eligible (go activate, 2 minutes) versus not assigned at all (file a request with the PIM owner, days). The remediation text says 'Activate one of' even when the operator cannot. Graph exposes the eligibility set to the user for themself via `/roleManagement/directory/roleEligibilityScheduleInstances/filterByCurrentUser(on='principal')` (delegated `RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory`, or `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`), keyed by `roleDefinitionId` which equals the built-in `roleTemplateId` the catalog already matches on. The readiness page is the app's stated answer to 'why can't I do X', and 'you are eligible — activate here' is the answer it is one call short of giving. The whole page already runs three planes concurrently (readiness.rs:73), so a fourth best-effort probe fits the existing degrade-to-'?' pattern.

Degrade to today's behaviour when the scope is unconsented. Table tests in readiness.rs alongside `directory_role_absent_is_missing_and_lists_alternatives`.
