findings.title: Multi-tenant work requires an app relaunch per tenant: settings hold one client/tenant pair and the auth service is constructed for a single tenant
findings.rationale: The 0.30.0 CHANGELOG itself names the persona: 'a consultant working several tenants had to re-point the app from outside the UI', and the fix was a Settings tab that saves the pair and relaunches. Everything below the auth service is already multi-tenant by construction — `graph_for(&tenant_id)`/`exchange_clients` are per-tenant maps, every cache key is `{tenant_id}|…`, `TenantScopedUi::reset()` and the open-items dock are keyed by tenant, and `tenant_defaults` in `settings.json` is a `BTreeMap<tenant_id, TenantDefaults>` — so the only single-tenant components are `UserSettings.{client_id,tenant_id}`, `AppState::new` resolving them once (state.rs:235-260), and `EntraAuthService::new(client_id, tenant_id)`. An MSP or multi-region admin switching between three tenants several times a day pays a full process restart, a browser round trip, and loses the audit run each time. This is the 'multi-tenant quick switch' item, verified absent.
findings.proposal: (L) Replace the single pair with `UserSettings.tenants: Vec<TenantProfile { label, client_id, tenant_id, cloud }>` plus `active_profile`, keep the two legacy fields as a migration source; make `EntraAuthService` hold per-tenant `(client_id, authority)` so `sign_in(profile)`/`restore_session` can target any profile, keyed in the keyring by `{tenant}:{oid}` exactly as today; expose `list_tenant_profiles`/`switch_tenant_profile`; in the frontend add a tenant switcher to the account menu that calls `session.set_active_tenant` (which already resets tenant-scoped UI and restores that tenant's parked dock). Keep the per-build baked pair as the single implicit profile so team builds are unchanged. Expected effect: switching tenants becomes a menu action with the existing cache-isolation guarantees, no relaunch.

findings.title: Audit never reads federated identity credentials, so a planted or over-broad OIDC trust is invisible in the security workbench
findings.rationale: The codebase's own module doc explains why a FIC is the most dangerous credential to miss: no secret, no expiry, silently accepted by Graph even when wrong. The audit scores secrets and certificates (Rules 5-9, 17) and even flags 'Uses client secret(s)' as a hygiene nudge toward federation, yet it never looks at the federated credentials an app already has — so an attacker-planted trust (`iss` = a GitHub org the tenant does not own, or a `sub` matching every branch via a flexible FIC `claimsMatchingExpression`), or a FIC left behind after a repo was archived, produces a clean row. The batched per-app FIC read already exists for the backup path, so the audit can reuse it at the same fan-out cost class; the validation rules in `core::federation` give the classifier.
findings.proposal: (M) In `run_audit`, fetch FICs per app through the backup's batched reader (only for apps that hold app permissions or admin-consented scopes, to bound cost), pass `federated: Vec<FederatedIdentityCredential>` into `score_application`, add advisory Rule 21: list issuers/subjects; flag `claimsMatchingExpression` present, issuers outside a per-tenant allowlist in `TenantDefaults` (e.g. `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` with an org prefix, the tenant's AKS OIDC issuer URL), and `sub` values without a ref/environment constraint. New `issue::FEDERATED_TRUST_REVIEW` marker + finding group (no one-click fix — admin-judged). CSV/JSON export columns. Table tests with the fixtures in `client/tests/credentials.rs`. Expected effect: the workbench sees the credential class its own docs call the worst case.

wire.rs:13-23 derives Debug on TokenResponse with plaintext access/refresh/id tokens. The convention is real and repeatedly applied: hand-written redacting Debug on AccessToken (token_cache.rs:107-110), PasswordCredential (core/models.rs:273), SelfSignedCertificate (models.rs:940), SecretValue/SecretSetRequest (keyvault/models.rs:57/95), KvSecretValueDto/KvSetSecretInput (dto/keyvault.rs:72/106), RegeneratedSecret (dto/backup.rs:486), OidcSsoSummary (dto/sso.rs:252), GeneratedCertificateResult (dto/applications.rs:255), GeneratedCert (cert.rs:66), each with a `<redacted>` test. Low severity is honest. `TokenErrorBody` (wire.rs:25) needs no change.

Premise verified: loopback.rs:86-99 writes the 200 'sign-in complete' page before any validation, then 100-106 returns on any `error` or mismatched `state`, so one forged request to the ephemeral port aborts the flow; dto/lib.rs:153-175 maps AuthError::Authorization via `err.to_string()`, so the attacker-chosen `error` text does reach the UI message. Existing test `state_mismatch_is_rejected` (loopback.rs:245-257) pins the current abort behaviour. Overstated: RFC 8252 discusses loopback interception risk but does not literally prescribe ignoring mismatched-state requests; the practical impact is a local DoS of one sign-in attempt by a process that knows the ephemeral port within the 300 s window. Trade-off the proposal omits: continuing the loop on mismatch means a genuine CSRF/mismatch now waits out the 300 s timeout instead of failing fast — acceptable, but it should be a deliberate choice with a warn! log.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Validate `state == expected_state` before writing any response; on mismatch (or an `error` without a matching state) answer 400, log at warn, and `continue` the accept loop. Only after the state matches, branch on `error` vs `code` and write the success/failure page; constrain the surfaced `error` to `[a-z_]+`. Update `state_mismatch_is_rejected` to assert the genuine redirect is still delivered afterwards, and accept that a real mismatch now surfaces as the 300 s timeout.

verdicts.notes: Verified: graph transport.rs:597-618 captures the raw body into Forbidden/NotFound/Api; arm/transport.rs:77-113 and keyvault/client.rs:213-244 do the same; only exchange transport.rs:293-324 sanitizes. The shared `http_error_enum!` Display (core/http_error.rs:70-81) interpolates the body, so `UiError::from` (dto/lib.rs:140-153, `err.to_string()`) shows it in toasts and `?err` logs (e.g. audit.rs:1497) write it to the rolling file verbatim. Nuance: DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351 and .claude/rules/auth.md:23 explicitly scope the sanitization claim to Exchange bodies, so this is a consistency gap in the 'never a raw body' rule rather than a doc contradiction; graph_err.rs:64-79 rewrites 403 bodies only on the scoped-feature paths. Moving the helper to core matches the 'one definition per policy' convention. Low severity is honest.

Premise verified: lib.rs:339-340 `create_dir_all(&log_dir)` (and lib.rs:32 for the config dir) leave the mode to the umask, while private_file.rs:12-16/71-75 makes settings.json and exports 0600 with an explicit rationale. Overstated: on macOS `~/Library` is 0700 by default, so `~/Library/Application Support/azapptoolkit/logs` is already owner-only there; on Linux many distros now create homes 0750 (Ubuntu >= 21.04), so exposure is limited to 755-home setups. tracing_appender files remain 0644, but a 0700 directory is sufficient. No doc or test covers log-directory permissions. Severity low holds.
verdicts.corrected_title: Log (and config) directory is created with the process umask while every file the app writes is owner-only

verdicts.corrected_title: tauri-sys git pin predates an upstream workaround for a reported (open, unconfirmed) wasm-bindgen function-table exhaustion in event deserialization
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Bump apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:33 to upstream v2 rev 1ffc6fa (or head 571cef4), regenerate web-rs/Cargo.lock, and run `just web-itest`. Blast radius is small: the diff only adds `T: 'static` bounds on invoke/invoke_result, a new `error::Deserialize` type, and `serde_json`/`tracing` deps (serde_json 1.0.151 and log 0.4.34 are already in the web-rs lock; wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 satisfies the new 0.2.127 floor). Note the upstream change also stops panicking on an undeserializable event (now `log::error!`, which no web-rs subscriber prints) — record that behaviour change next to the pin. Add a review date to the pin comment and, if desired, a `just deps-git-status` recipe (`git ls-remote` + commits ahead of the rev); the existing informal practice is the release-time check recorded in docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:127.
verdicts.notes: Evidence verified. Pinned checkout (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tauri-sys-*/289bd29) has `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap()` inside the listener Closure at src/event.rs:137 and :184, and in core.rs:14,25-26,126. A bare clone of upstream v2 shows exactly four commits after the pin; 1ffc6fa (2026-09-08, 'Update conversion of JsValues (#113)', bumps 0.2.4→0.2.5) adds lib.rs `from_value` that does `js_sys::JSON::stringify` + `serde_json::from_str` with the comment 'must serialize and deserialize to prevent overflowing wasm method table, see wasm-bindgen/issues/5324'. Fetched issue #5324: title matches, OPENED 2026-09-06, still OPEN, Tauri+Leptos+tauri-sys, error 'RuntimeError: Out of bounds table access'; the root-cause claim ('from_value creates a new WASM function for every field') is the reporter's own analysis with no maintainer comment, and wasm-bindgen 0.2.129's CHANGELOG (our lock) has no fix. Our exposure is real: 8 `listen::<..>` streams in web-rs/src/bindings/events.rs:19-77, consumed via hooks/use_progress_stream.rs for the component's lifetime, and the backend emits once per app (audit.rs:346,419; bulk.rs:993). Overstated: severity 'high' for an unreproduced, single-reporter, still-open issue whose mechanism the wasm-bindgen maintainers have not confirmed; 'the fix is upstream' (it is a workaround in tauri-sys, not a fix); and 'no reminder mechanism' (the pin is re-checked at release time, see CHANGELOG-archive.md:127, just not automated). Dependabot's inability to bump a git rev was not verifiable offline. The pin comment itself ('Bump deliberately') makes a deliberate bump on-convention.

Cargo.toml:43 `keyring-core = { package = "keyring_core", version = "1.0" }` is real; the only consumer, crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:20, declares `keyring-core = "1.0"` directly, so the workspace entry is dead (introduced with PR #219, commit 06af5cc). Reproduced the resolution failure offline in a scratch manifest: `cargo metadata` with `package = "keyring_core"` → 'no matching package found / searched package name: `keyring_core` / perhaps you meant: keyring-core' (cargo does not normalise `-`/`_` in `package =`). Cargo.lock:2655 holds `keyring-core 1.0.0`. Nothing pins workspace-dependency consistency (tests/dependency_policy.rs only checks advisory-ignore sync). Severity lowered from medium: nothing is broken today, and the failure mode is loud and self-diagnosing at resolve time; it only fires when someone follows the AGENTS.md workspace-dependency rule.

Verified with `cargo tree --locked --offline -p desktop -e features -i reqwest`: `reqwest feature "system-proxy"` is reached only through `tauri-plugin-updater feature "system-proxy"` ← `tauri-plugin-updater feature "default"`; the workspace declaration (Cargo.toml:29) lists only rustls/json/query/form, and reqwest-0.13.5's `default` (dropped by `default-features = false`) is what would otherwise carry `system-proxy`. tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0 `default = ["rustls-tls", "system-proxy", "zip"]` confirmed. None of our seven `reqwest::Client::builder()` sites (graph/client.rs:163, exchange/client.rs:74, keyvault/client.rs:54, arm/client.rs:36, arm/loganalytics.rs:27, auth/service/mod.rs:93, sso/mod.rs:1282) sets or disables a proxy, so OS-proxy discovery is indeed inherited. No doc, comment or test records this. The proposal is zero-cost (feature already unified in) and fits the repo's habit of stating feature choices explicitly (see the oauth2/base64 blocks). Severity lowered from medium: it is a latent fragility, not a present defect, and the trigger (someone trimming the updater's defaults or a plugin default change) is speculative; the value is that the regression would be invisible to CI.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43 declare anyhow and thiserror; `grep -rn 'anyhow\|thiserror'` over src-tauri/src, tests and build.rs returns nothing, and src-tauri does not invoke `http_error_enum!` (callers are only arm/graph/keyvault error.rs:10), so neither is needed even via macro expansion. `cargo tree -i anyhow --depth 1` confirms `desktop` is the only workspace member depending on anyhow (other edges are tauri, tauri-build, tauri-plugin, tauri-plugin-fs, tauri-utils), so Cargo.toml:51 `anyhow = "1"` can go too. Severity lowered from medium to low: manifest hygiene with no runtime or build effect.

verdicts.corrected_title: tracing declared but never used in azapptoolkit-keyvault, azapptoolkit-arm and web-rs
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Remove the three declarations (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20, crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19, apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63). Do NOT add tracing::warn! calls to the keyvault/arm transports: both already route every request through `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::with_retries` (keyvault/src/client.rs:175, arm/src/transport.rs:43), which emits the `tracing::warn!(attempt, label, retry_after_secs, "transient failure; retrying")` at core/src/http_retry.rs:207 — adding per-crate logging would duplicate the one shared retry policy. For web-rs, if browser-side tracing is ever wanted, add a console subscriber deliberately and document it in frontend-workspace.md.
verdicts.notes: Premise true: `grep -rn tracing` over keyvault/src, arm/src, web-rs/src, web-rs/tests and web-rs/build.rs returns nothing, and no subscriber is installed in the WASM bundle. Overstated rationale: 'the asymmetry hides that these two clients emit nothing on 429/5xx' is wrong — Key Vault and ARM (control plane and Log Analytics) use core's `with_retries`, which logs throttles/5xx centrally, so their silence is by design under AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule. verdicts.corrected_title: No unused-dependency gate in verify-full/CI; five dead declarations slipped through
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add a `just udeps` recipe running `cargo machete --with-metadata` over the root and `apps/desktop/web-rs`, wire it into `verify-full` AND the `deny` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (the `verify_full_runs_every_gate_ci_runs` test pins the two to each other), pinning the tool version via taiki-e/install-action like cargo-deny@0.20.2. Ship it with `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` in graph/arm/keyvault from day one — the re-export refactor in finding [6] cannot be taken (thiserror's derive hard-codes `::thiserror::__private` paths), so those three declarations are permanently macro-only and will always read as unused.
verdicts.notes: Premise true: `grep -i 'udeps\|machete\|shear'` over justfile, ci.yml, docs/, AGENTS.md and .claude/ finds nothing; justfile:334-355 gate only audit/deny; ci.yml:268-290 `deny` job installs `just,cargo-deny@0.20.2`. The dead-declaration count is 5 unique manifest lines (anyhow+thiserror in src-tauri, tracing ×3), not 6. Feasible: async-trait is imported as `use async_trait::async_trait;` (core/src/token.rs:9) and every web-rs dep has textual `name::` use, so false positives are limited to the macro-expanded thiserror in the three `http_error_enum!` callers. verdicts.corrected_title: http_error_enum! expands to ::thiserror::Error, so its three callers must declare thiserror with no textual use — undocumented in their manifests
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Keep `thiserror = { workspace = true }` in graph/arm/keyvault (it is genuinely required) and add a one-line comment at each (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/Cargo.toml:21, arm:18, keyvault:19): 'no textual use — required by the derive `azapptoolkit_core::http_error_enum!` expands to; do not remove'. Add the same note to the macro's doc comment in core/src/http_error.rs. Optionally add `thiserror = { workspace = true }` to core so the crate owning the taxonomy also declares it. If cargo-machete is adopted (finding [5]), add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to the three callers.
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: core/src/http_error.rs:65 `#[derive(Debug, ::thiserror::Error)]`, core's Cargo.toml has no thiserror, and graph/arm/keyvault (error.rs:10 each) declare it with no other use. But the proposed `$crate::thiserror::Error` re-export does NOT work: thiserror-impl 2.0.x's expansion hard-codes absolute `::thiserror::__private::...` paths in the generated code (registry thiserror-impl-2.0.18/src/expand.rs:212 `impl ... ::thiserror::#private::Error for #ty`, :68 `use ::thiserror::#private::AsDynError`, :39/:49 inferred bounds), and thiserror has no crate-path attribute (none in thiserror-impl/src/attr.rs). Since expansion happens in the caller's crate, each caller must have `thiserror` in its extern prelude regardless of how the derive is named — dropping the lines would fail exactly as the finding fears, and the refactor would too. The phantom dependency is a thiserror limitation, not a hygiene lapse; the actionable part is documentation.

Verified: `bytes = "1"` at crates/azapptoolkit-{graph,exchange,keyvault,arm}/Cargo.toml:14, used as `bytes::Bytes` return types in each transport (graph/transport.rs:126,438,455,494,520,537; exchange/transport.rs:154; keyvault/client.rs:136; arm/client.rs:242, arm/transport.rs:32); no `bytes` entry in Cargo.toml:24-68 `[workspace.dependencies]`. Four identical inline requirements is what the AGENTS.md 'Workspace dependency' pattern and .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md exist to centralise; the change is mechanical with no lockfile effect. The `webbrowser` aside is optional: the rule does not require single-consumer deps to be workspace-managed (src-tauri keeps rcgen, aws-lc-rs, p12-keystore, rand and time inline by design), so treat that as uniformity, not a rule violation.

Verified: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:88 `time = "0.3"` sits under the heavily-commented crypto block (rcgen, aws-lc-rs, p12-keystore each carry rationale) with no comment; cert.rs:22 `use time::{Duration, OffsetDateTime}`, :54 `pub not_after: OffsetDateTime`, :119-121 sets rcgen's `not_before`/`not_after`; credentials.rs:140-141 round-trips through `unix_timestamp()` into chrono. The only other consumer of `GeneratedCert.not_after` is the unit test at cert.rs:261 (`> OffsetDateTime::now_utc()`), which would move to chrono trivially. chrono is already a src-tauri dep (Cargo.toml:39). `time 0.3.55` stays in the graph via rcgen/x509-parser/cookie regardless, so this is about manifest clarity and keeping the second date library private to cert.rs. No architecture doc mentions the `time` crate (grep of docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md). Proposal feasible and low-risk.

Sites verified: token_cache.rs:11 `use parking_lot::RwLock` vs :239 `static CHUNK_SET_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()>` + :246-248 poison-recovery guard; core/settings.rs:116-120 std Mutex with poison-recovery prose; src-tauri/commands/throttle.rs:37 std Mutex while state.rs:12 uses parking_lot; parking_lot RwLock at graph/client.rs:143. Feasibility checked: core's `parking_lot` is gated `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` (core/Cargo.toml:23) and `settings` is gated the same way (core/src/lib.rs:29-30), so it is available there; parking_lot 0.12's `Mutex::new` is const, so both `static` sites can switch. `cargo tree -i parking_lot` confirms tao keeps it in the graph, so nothing is gained by going the other way either. verdicts.corrected_title: Workspace tokio feature set is the union; library crates inherit net/io-util/rt-multi-thread/macros they don't use
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Set the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:26) to `features = ["sync", "time"]`. In crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml add `features = ["net", "io-util", "rt"]` — `rt` is required by the non-test `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` at service/mod.rs:457 and :509, not only the loopback listener — and add `[dev-dependencies] tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt"] }` (auth currently has no tokio dev-dep and its 7 `#[tokio::test]`s in loopback.rs and service/mod.rs ride the workspace `macros`/`rt-multi-thread`). In apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml add `features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"]` (tokio::join! at enterprise_application.rs:131, backup.rs:368,519, readiness.rs:76, sso/mod.rs:466; tokio::spawn in five commands). graph/exchange/keyvault/arm/core already carry `macros`/`rt` dev-deps and use only tokio::sync/time in src.
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: Cargo.toml:26 enables macros, rt-multi-thread, sync, time, net, io-util; only auth uses tokio::net/io (loopback.rs:7-8, service/mod.rs:34); no `Runtime::new`/`#[tokio::main]` anywhere (runtime is Tauri's); graph/exchange/keyvault/arm src use no tokio API beyond what tests need; core uses only tokio::time (http_retry.rs, cache). Overstated/incomplete: the proposal's auth feature set omits `rt`, which `spawn_blocking` (auth/service/mod.rs:457,509 — keyring I/O deliberately moved off the async worker) needs, and omits the dev-dependency auth would need for its `#[tokio::test]`s; as written the trim would break auth's build and tests. Value is precision only (feature unification leaves the shipped binary unchanged), so low.

verdicts.corrected_title: The futures facade's default `executor` feature pulls futures-executor into Windows/macOS builds for nothing
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Change the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:27) to `futures = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["std", "async-await"] }`. futures-0.3.34's `default = ["std", "async-await", "executor"]` and `executor = ["std", "futures-executor/std"]`, so dropping the default removes futures-executor with ZERO source changes — every item used (future::{join, join4, join_all, try_join}, stream::{self, StreamExt, FuturesUnordered}, `join!`, future::abortable) is re-exported by the facade under std+async-await. Confirm with `cargo tree -e normal,build -i futures-executor --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (today it prints `futures-executor ← futures` only). Rewriting ~30 `futures::` paths to `futures_util::` buys nothing extra.
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: `cargo tree --locked --offline -i futures-executor` → `futures v0.3.34` (← azapptoolkit-graph, desktop, and wiremock dev-only) plus `glib v0.18.5` (Linux GTK); with `-e normal,build --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` futures-executor is present solely via `futures`. All 25 use sites in graph/src/client/batch.rs:138 and src-tauri commands are futures-util items. Overstated: the switch-to-futures-util proposal is far more churn than needed; the facade's own feature flags achieve the same drop, matching how the repo already handles oauth2/base64/reqwest (`default-features = false` + explicit features with a comment). web-rs is correctly excluded (tauri-sys depends on the facade with defaults).
